note: Which parameters the signature parse marks as hydrated to Date. The truthiness rule and the hydration itself are the step runner's (C3a).

given.source: type Ts = Date; export function main(d: Ts) { return d instanceof Date; }

cases.title: a three-member union is not hydrated

given.source: export function main(d: Date | null | undefined) { return typeof d; }
export function main(ds: Date[]) { return typeof ds[0]; }

cases.title: Date and a two-member union with undefined are hydrated; Base64 and Uint8Array are not
cases.rest_in: C3a applies the truthiness rule (WR-8/d to WR-8/f use this script)

given.source: export function main(d: Date, e: Date | undefined, s: Base64, u: Uint8Array) { return [d instanceof Date ? d.toISOString() : String(d), e === undefined, typeof s, Array.isArray(u)]; }

cases.title: an optional Date parameter, and one with a default

given.source: export function main(d?: Date, e: Date = new Date(0)) { return [d, e]; }

cases.title: a two-member union with null, in either order, and parentheses

given.source: export function main(a: null | Date, b: (Date | null), c: (Date)) { return [a, b, c]; }

cases.title: aliases resolve recursively, wherever they are declared, exported ones included
other unions, interfaces, imported names, missing annotations and arrays are not hydrated
the name Date is matched before a local alias of that name

given.source:
type Date = string;
export function main(d: Date) { return d; }

cases.title: aliases that refer to each other resolve to nothing
cases.note: The reference does not cover aliases that refer to each other; they resolve to no type here.

cases.title: a qualified globalThis.Date is not the name Date
cases.note: The reference matches the type reference Date by name; a qualified name is read as another reference (open question in the PR).

given.source: export function main(d: globalThis.Date) { return d; }

cases.title: aliases are looked up by their snake-case name
cases.note: The reference spelling MyDate and my_date share the snake-case name my_date.

given.source:
type MyDate = Date;
export function main(d: my_date) { return d; }
